9o2edc.q: The broken white line shown can be crossed
9o2edc.why: A broken line is not a prohibition: you may cross it to overtake, turn or change lane when it is safe.

h6ewup.q: The broken white line shown divides the carriageway into two lanes
h6ewup.why: A broken line separates the lanes of one carriageway, and it can be crossed.

zg6tm1.q: On two-way roads with two lanes, the broken white line shown divides the directions of travel
zg6tm1.why: On a two-lane two-way road, the broken centre line (mezzeria) separates the two directions of travel.

6c1yi1.q: The broken white line shown allows you, when you want to overtake, to temporarily occupy the other lane
6c1yi1.why: Because it is broken, you may briefly use the other lane to overtake, provided nothing else forbids it.

6fuzh9.q: The broken white line shown allows a U-turn, in safe conditions, if the road is two-way
6fuzh9.why: On a two-way road a broken line allows a U-turn (inversione di marcia) if it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

1dwy5ls.q: The broken white line shown allows a left turn
1dwy5ls.why: A broken line may be crossed, so it allows you to turn left safely.

17gl11r.q: On a one-way carriageway, the broken white line shown serves to delimit the lanes
17gl11r.why: On a one-way road the broken line separates lanes that all travel in the same direction.

1tjlvb4.q: The broken white line shown, on one-way roads, divides the lanes
1tjlvb4.why: On one-way roads the broken line divides the lanes.

6ya8do.q: The broken white line shown allows you to drive straddling it
6ya8do.why: You may cross a broken line only briefly; driving straddling it is not allowed.

1dee3mo.q: The broken white line shown separates the road from a cycle lane
1dee3mo.why: The line shown runs along the carriageway and divides lanes or directions of travel, not a cycle path.

14jz15o.q: The broken white line shown is found near all level crossings
14jz15o.why: Near level crossings you find a continuous line that forbids overtaking, not a broken one.

1si926b.q: The broken white line shown can be replaced by a series of road studs ("chiodi")
1si926b.why: Road studs or reflectors may supplement road markings but cannot replace the broken line.

146zf6x.q: The broken white line shown allows a U-turn on one-way roads
146zf6x.why: On one-way roads a U-turn is forbidden, even where the line is broken.

y8yog7.q: The broken white line shown divides the road into two carriageways, each two-way
y8yog7.why: It divides a single carriageway (carreggiata) into two lanes, not into two separate carriageways.

77qfda.q: The broken white line shown is found only on one-way roads
77qfda.why: The broken line is also found on two-way roads, where it separates the two directions of travel.

wmft5i.q: On one-way roads the broken white line shown is placed on hill crests to divide the two directions of travel
wmft5i.why: On hill crests a continuous line is used, and a one-way road has no opposing directions to divide.

zjcu8c.q: Lines along the centre of the carriageway may be crossed if they are broken (dashed)
zjcu8c.why: Broken centre lines may be crossed to overtake, turn or make a U-turn.

8vnp47.q: Lines along the centre of the carriageway may not be crossed if they are continuous
8vnp47.why: A continuous centre line must not be crossed.

d6e8lt.q: The central line shown allows overtaking without crossing it, provided nothing else forbids it
d6e8lt.why: You cannot cross a continuous line, but you may overtake without crossing it if nothing else forbids it.

14gx79m.q: The double line shown cannot be crossed, but you may drive straddling it
14gx79m.why: A double continuous line cannot be crossed, and driving straddling it is also forbidden.

124035w.q: Lines along the centre of the carriageway can be white or light blue
124035w.why: Centre lines are always white; light blue is used only for paid parking bays.

2p8z8d.q: The broken line shown can be replaced with a few road studs or reflectors placed 50 centimetres apart
2p8z8d.why: Studs or reflectors can only supplement road markings, not replace the line.

1gngdte.q: The central line shown does not allow overtaking in any case
1gngdte.why: A continuous line forbids crossing it, not overtaking itself: you may overtake without crossing it.

18zkfht.q: The double continuous line shown serves to divide the directions of travel on two-way roads
18zkfht.why: A double continuous line separates the two directions of travel on two-way roads.

6wrqfl.q: The double continuous line shown cannot be crossed
6wrqfl.why: A double continuous line may never be crossed.

1jaom60.q: The double continuous line shown allows overtaking, where permitted, without crossing it
1jaom60.why: You may overtake where permitted only if you do not cross the double continuous line.

783hq5.q: The double continuous line shown does not allow reversing direction (U-turn)
783hq5.why: You cannot cross a double continuous line, so a U-turn is forbidden.

1a2ktlm.q: The double continuous line shown does not allow turning left
1a2ktlm.why: Turning left would mean crossing the double continuous line, which is forbidden.

1mr73fn.q: The double continuous line shown can be found at the edges of the road, to mark its margins
1mr73fn.why: Road edges are marked with a single line; a double continuous line divides opposing traffic in the middle.

1upms5s.q: The double continuous line shown indicates that you may travel in parallel lines
1upms5s.why: It separates the two directions of travel; it does not mean you may drive in parallel lanes.

ewpe9o.q: The double continuous line shown marks the point where drivers must stop because of a STOP sign
ewpe9o.why: The stop line at a STOP sign is a single transverse continuous line, not a double longitudinal one.

1gyes9g.q: The double continuous line shown is light blue in paid parking areas
1gyes9g.why: A double continuous centre line is white; light blue applies only to paid parking bays.

xe9f66.q: The double continuous line shown can be crossed
xe9f66.why: A double continuous line can never be crossed.

13sa0n4.q: The guide stripes shown are curved, broken (dashed) white lines
13sa0n4.why: Guide stripes are curved, broken white lines showing the path to follow when turning.

tcdqsu.q: The guide stripes shown are normally found where a left turn is made leaving the centre of the junction on our right
tcdqsu.why: They guide left turns, which are made leaving the centre of the junction on your right.

18a4cxx.q: The guide stripes shown must be left on the left of the vehicle when turning left
18a4cxx.why: When turning left you follow the path marked by the guide stripes without entering the opposite lane.

efrnjn.q: The guide stripes shown serve to make the turn correctly, without taking the road on the left against the flow
efrnjn.why: They show the correct path for turning, preventing you from entering the left-hand road against the traffic flow.

idszjj.q: The guide stripes shown must always be left on the right of the vehicle when turning right
idszjj.why: Guide stripes are for left turns; this rule does not apply when turning right.

1suzpgg.q: The guide stripes shown cannot be crossed by vehicles continuing straight
1suzpgg.why: Being broken, they may be crossed by vehicles going straight ahead.

19dwhqg.q: The guide stripes shown delimit a traffic island
19dwhqg.why: They are only broken path markings, not the boundary of a traffic island (isola di traffico).

19iylmp.q: The directional arrows shown are found inside the lanes, before a junction
19iylmp.why: Directional arrows are painted inside the lanes before a junction.

1qe5z9w.q: The directional arrows shown indicate to drivers the directions allowed at the junction
1qe5z9w.why: Directional arrows show which directions each lane may take at the junction.

rbi1qi.q: The directional arrows shown allow you to move into the chosen lane while the lane lines are still broken (dashed)
rbi1qi.why: While the lane lines are still broken, you may change lanes to reach the one you need.

15s701a.q: The directional arrows shown oblige you to follow the direction indicated if the lane lines are continuous
15s701a.why: With continuous lane lines you cannot change lanes, so the indicated direction is compulsory.

2sv9w0.q: The directional arrows shown are combined straight-right arrows for lanes meant for those going straight or right
2sv9w0.why: The combined straight-right arrow marks lanes for traffic going straight or turning right.

1ud616a.q: The directional arrows shown can be accompanied by writing on the road surface indicating the destination reachable
1ud616a.why: Arrows may be supplemented by road-surface lettering naming the places reached.

os50wb.q: The directional arrows shown indicate the permitted directions
os50wb.why: Directional arrows indicate the directions permitted from the lane.

dlpfcd.q: The directional arrows shown oblige you to follow the direction indicated, even if the lane lines are broken (dashed)
dlpfcd.why: With broken lines you can still change lanes; the obligation applies only when the lines are continuous.

2d5q8h.q: The directional arrows shown indicate that you are near an emergency stopping lane
2d5q8h.why: Directional arrows show permitted directions, not an emergency lane ahead.

13gtl7b.q: The directional arrows shown allow us to change lane if the lines are continuous
13gtl7b.why: Continuous lines cannot be crossed, so you may not change lane.

8ysju7.q: The directional arrows shown are light blue to indicate paid parking
8ysju7.why: Directional arrows are always white; light blue is for paid parking bays.

1gn44gt.q: The directional arrows shown are yellow on roads where parking is prohibited
1gn44gt.why: Directional arrows are always white, never yellow.

1ij5q14.q: The directional arrows shown are blue on motorways
1ij5q14.why: Directional arrows are white, including on motorways.

ua7617.q: The traffic island shown indicates a stretch of road closed to the passage and parking of vehicles
ua7617.why: A traffic island (isola di traffico) marked with diagonal stripes is closed to both passing and parking.

2vpm4u.q: The traffic island shown is made with oblique white stripes
2vpm4u.why: A traffic island is made of oblique white stripes bounded by continuous lines.

plhiml.q: The traffic island shown indicates a part of the road on which you cannot travel
plhiml.why: You may not drive on a traffic island; vehicles must go around it.

1rnj74c.q: With the traffic island shown, vehicle C must turn right
1rnj74c.why: Since the island cannot be entered, vehicle C must turn right, following the road layout.

1pswuy1.q: With the traffic island shown, vehicle B must turn right
1pswuy1.why: B cannot drive over the island, so it must turn right.

5lgjqc.q: With the traffic island shown, vehicle A must go straight on
5lgjqc.why: A cannot cross the island, so it must go straight on.

1661nd.q: The traffic island shown can also be made with light blue transverse stripes
1661nd.why: Traffic islands are always white oblique stripes; light blue is not used.

b0ke4t.q: The traffic island shown indicates an area where vehicles may park
b0ke4t.why: Both parking and driving are forbidden on a traffic island.

1opv335.q: The traffic island shown indicates a part of the carriageway where you may stop for only 30 minutes
1opv335.why: On a traffic island you may neither drive nor park, not even for 30 minutes.

1j1nis2.q: With the traffic island shown, vehicle C may go in any direction
1j1nis2.why: The island cannot be driven on, so C has only one permitted direction.

1oloisf.q: With the traffic island shown, vehicle B may turn left, giving way to vehicle A
1oloisf.why: B must turn right; the island prevents a left turn even if B gives way.

e5p534.q: With the traffic island shown, vehicle A may turn left, giving way to vehicle C
e5p534.why: A must go straight; the island does not allow a left turn even if A gives way.

zlcnb9.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the central continuous line shown is found before a bend
zlcnb9.why: A continuous centre line is placed before a bend, where visibility is limited.

1qmskkb.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the central continuous line shown is found on the uphill part of a hill crest
1qmskkb.why: On the uphill side of a crest (dosso) visibility is poor, so a continuous line is used.

7h29n1.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the central continuous line shown is found before a junction
7h29n1.why: A continuous line is placed before a junction to prevent dangerous overtaking.

11bjnyp.q: The vehicle shown cannot cross the central continuous line
11bjnyp.why: The continuous line is on the vehicle's side, so it cannot cross it.

2m7ash.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the central continuous line shown is normally found on one-way roads
2m7ash.why: A central line divides two directions of travel, so it is on two-way roads.

ljdi0r.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the central continuous line shown is found every time you pass the downhill part of a hill crest
ljdi0r.why: It is not found every time: on the downhill side of a crest it may be broken, since visibility returns.

1pl86sc.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the central continuous line shown is found every time you pass a level crossing
1pl86sc.why: The continuous line is used before a level crossing, not after you have passed it.

205iv5.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the central continuous line shown allows reversing direction
205iv5.why: A continuous line cannot be crossed, so a U-turn is forbidden.

10bnm5f.q: The vehicle shown may overtake even by crossing the central continuous line
10bnm5f.why: With the continuous line on its side, the vehicle may overtake only without crossing it.

1iiog52.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown is found just after a bend
1iiog52.why: After the bend visibility is good again, so the line is broken for this vehicle.

8yszva.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown allows overtaking even by crossing both lines
8yszva.why: With the broken line on its side, the vehicle may cross both lines to overtake.

w74uy.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown is found after a level crossing
w74uy.why: After the level crossing the line becomes broken again for vehicles moving away.

19fmej9.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown can be found on the downhill part of a hill crest
19fmej9.why: On the downhill side of a crest visibility is good, so the line can be broken.

1d2kr6r.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown also allows the oncoming vehicle to cross the lines
1d2kr6r.why: For the oncoming vehicle the continuous line is on its side, so it cannot cross.

xkv2je.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown is normally found on one-way roads
xkv2je.why: The paired lines divide two directions of travel, so they are on two-way roads.

wmyomg.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown is found on the uphill part of a hill crest
wmyomg.why: On the uphill side of a crest visibility is poor and the line is continuous, not broken.

vx761k.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown is found just before a junction
vx761k.why: Before a junction the line is continuous; the broken one comes after.

1lheqam.q: Relative to the vehicle moving in the direction of the arrow, the broken line shown is found before a bend
1lheqam.why: Before a bend visibility is limited, so the line is continuous.

er1uvm.q: The yellow and black marks shown, painted on the kerb edge, indicate a parking prohibition
er1uvm.why: Yellow and black marks on the kerb mean no parking.

5ayg67.q: The yellow and black marks shown are placed along the vertical part of the kerb
5ayg67.why: The yellow and black marks are painted on the vertical face of the kerb.

1v2zqni.q: The yellow and black marks shown, painted on the kerb edge, indicate that parking is not possible on that side of the road
1v2zqni.why: Parking is prohibited on that side of the road.

18yewfu.q: The yellow and black marks shown, painted on the kerb edge, allow stopping
18yewfu.why: The ban is on parking (sosta); a brief stop (fermata) is allowed.

r8w9i8.q: The yellow and black marks in the figure painted on the edge of the sidewalk indicate that parking is allowed only for buses
r8w9i8.why: A yellow and black kerb (bordo del marciapiede) bans parking for every vehicle. It does not reserve the space for buses.

j4iyy6.q: The yellow and black marks in the figure painted on the edge of the sidewalk signal an obstacle in the middle of the carriageway
j4iyy6.why: Yellow and black kerb marks are a parking ban. They do not warn of an obstacle in the carriageway.

am996m.q: The yellow and black marks in the figure painted on the edge of the sidewalk warn pedestrians to watch out for the step
am996m.why: The yellow and black kerb is for drivers and means no parking. It is not a warning to pedestrians about a step.

xst890.q: The yellow and black marks in the figure painted on the edge of the sidewalk indicate that stopping is also prohibited
xst890.why: Yellow and black kerb marks ban only parking. Stopping briefly (fermata) is still allowed.

m4ijzc.q: The markings in the figure indicate a zone for stopping buses in scheduled public service
m4ijzc.why: The yellow zigzag line with the word BUS marks the stop area for buses in scheduled public service (servizio pubblico di linea).

ixklrm.q: The markings in the figure indicate the space for the stopping of buses and trolleybuses in scheduled public service
ixklrm.why: The yellow zigzag marking reserves the space for buses and trolleybuses (filobus) in scheduled public service to stop.

1ohlibg.q: The zigzag stripe of the markings in the figure helps buses with the manoeuvre of pulling up to the kerb and setting off again
1ohlibg.why: The zigzag zone keeps space free so the bus can pull in to the kerb and pull out again.

2hvdfq.q: The markings in the figure prohibit parking but not stopping, even in the parts with the yellow zigzag stripe
2hvdfq.why: In a bus stop zone, including where the yellow zigzag stripe is, parking (sosta) is banned but stopping (fermata) is not.

1a8r4sr.q: The markings in the figure indicate the space for the stopping of articulated buses in scheduled public service
1a8r4sr.why: The zigzag space is for scheduled public-service buses to stop, including articulated ones (autosnodati), which need more length.

18urjor.q: The markings in the figure indicate the space reserved for the parking of taxis as well
18urjor.why: This zone is for scheduled public buses only. Taxis have their own bays marked TAXI.

w77tf8.q: The markings in the figure do not allow cars to drive inside the marked area
w77tf8.why: The marking bans parking, not driving. Cars may pass through the area as long as they do not park.

c2joam.q: The markings in the figure do not allow parking 20 metres before the yellow zigzag stripe
c2joam.why: The ban applies only within the zone marked by the yellow zigzag stripe. There is no automatic 20-metre ban before it.

19rc9pm.q: The markings in the figure prohibit trucks from driving inside the marked area
19rc9pm.why: The bus stop zone bans parking, not traffic. Trucks (autocarri) may also drive through it.

1x748ze.q: The markings in the figure can also be made with white stripes
1x748ze.why: The bus stop zigzag is always yellow. White is not allowed for it.

15o0mp4.q: The markings in the figure allow cars to park from 8.00 p.m. to 8.00 a.m.
15o0mp4.why: The bus stop zone has no time windows. Parking stays banned at all hours.

1tgv31p.q: With the guide stripes shown in the figure, vehicle C may go straight ahead
1tgv31p.why: Guide stripes (strisce di guida) only show the path for turning. Vehicle C is not forced to turn and may go straight.

1duy2ra.q: With the guide stripes shown in the figure, vehicle B may turn left, but must give way to vehicle A
1duy2ra.why: B comes from the side road and may turn left along the stripes, but must give way to traffic on the main road such as A.

10hcgz0.q: With the guide stripes shown in the figure, vehicle A may go in any direction
10hcgz0.why: On the main road, A may go straight or turn into the side road. The stripes do not force a direction.

cdp9ik.q: With the guide stripes shown in the figure, vehicle C must turn right
cdp9ik.why: Guide stripes do not force a turn. C may turn, but may also continue straight on the main road.

1vy20g9.q: With the guide stripes shown in the figure, vehicle B must turn right
1vy20g9.why: Guide stripes do not force a right turn. B may also turn left, giving way.

1u21zb8.q: With the guide stripes shown in the figure, vehicle A must go straight ahead
1u21zb8.why: A is not obliged to go straight. The guide stripes also allow a turn into the side road.

ugmqnn.q: All three lanes shown in the figure allow the driver to continue straight ahead
ugmqnn.why: With no mandatory arrows, every lane lets the driver continue straight ahead, besides any turns allowed.

khzlr9.q: The left lane shown in the figure allows the driver to continue straight ahead or turn left
khzlr9.why: The left lane has no restrictive arrows, so the driver may go straight or turn left.

10ap5bc.q: The middle lane shown in the figure allows the driver only to continue straight ahead
10ap5bc.why: The middle lane, between the other two, is for going straight only.

1c1oi3w.q: The right lane shown in the figure allows the driver to continue straight ahead or turn right
1c1oi3w.why: The right lane has no restrictive arrows, so the driver may go straight or turn right.

173ttf.q: It is possible to change lanes as long as the lines are still dashed (broken)
173ttf.why: A dashed line (striscia discontinua) may be crossed to change lane. Once the line becomes continuous, it may not.

kf7d4s.q: The vehicle shown in the figure may turn left while staying in the same lane
kf7d4s.why: The vehicle is in the left lane, which allows a left turn, so it does not need to change lane.

5oqz5e.q: The left lane shown in the figure allows the driver only to turn left
5oqz5e.why: The left lane does not force a left turn. It also allows going straight.

8ovl1g.q: The right lane shown in the figure is reserved for slow vehicles
8ovl1g.why: No lane in the figure is reserved for slow vehicles. The right lane is for going straight or turning right.

pdvdl6.q: The right lane shown in the figure allows the driver only to turn right
pdvdl6.why: The right lane does not force a right turn. It also allows going straight.

p7yf17.q: With the road markings shown in the figure, the driver is allowed to change lanes even by crossing the continuous line
p7yf17.why: A continuous line (striscia continua) must not be crossed. Lane changes are allowed only where the line is dashed.

1c8h4e9.q: Lanes A, B and C shown in the figure do not allow the driver to continue straight ahead
1c8h4e9.why: The arrows show only turns: A left, B left or right, C right. No lane allows going straight.

18xbdpq.q: Lane A shown in the figure allows the driver to turn only to the left
18xbdpq.why: The arrow in lane A shows a left turn only.

dtf8gp.q: With the signs shown in the figure, the driver may change lanes where the lane lines are still dashed (broken)
dtf8gp.why: The arrows bind the driver only where the lines are continuous. Where they are still dashed, changing lanes is allowed.

ao5dj8.q: Lanes A, B and C shown in the figure are two-way
ao5dj8.why: The arrows all point the same way, so the lanes are one-way, not two-way.

vdgyg8.q: Lanes A, B and C shown in the figure allow the driver to go in all directions
vdgyg8.why: The arrows allow only turns. No lane allows going straight.

1iln10y.q: Lane B shown in the figure allows the driver to turn and to continue straight ahead
1iln10y.why: Lane B has arrows for left and right turns only. Going straight is not allowed.

1anzxkr.q: Lane A shown in the figure allows the driver only to turn left
1anzxkr.why: Lane A has left-turn arrows only.

nm9quz.q: Lane B shown in the figure allows the driver to continue straight ahead and to turn left
nm9quz.why: The arrows in lane B show both straight ahead and a left turn.

1m4xz5d.q: With the markings in the figure, lane C is the only one that allows turning right
1m4xz5d.why: Only lane C has a right-turn arrow. A and B allow only straight or left.

v3kovf.q: With the markings in the figure, it is allowed to change lanes as long as the lines are still dashed (broken)
v3kovf.why: While the lines are dashed (discontinue) you may change lane. Where they become continuous, your direction is fixed.

1gvjs0a.q: All three lanes shown in the figure allow the driver to continue straight ahead
1gvjs0a.why: Lane A has a left-turn arrow only, so it does not allow going straight.

p2d5.q: With the markings in the figure, lane A is the only one that allows turning left
p2d5.why: Lane B also has a left-turn arrow, besides straight ahead, so A is not the only one.

18waokm.q: Lane B shown in the figure allows the driver only to continue straight ahead
18waokm.why: Lane B also allows a left turn, as the arrows show.

w9ph4w.q: Lane C shown in the figure allows the driver only to turn right
w9ph4w.why: Lane C also allows going straight, as the arrows show.

5gwxwt.q: The kerb painted as shown in the figure prohibits parking for taxis as well
5gwxwt.why: The yellow and black kerb parking ban applies to all vehicles, taxis included.

130ye93.q: The kerb painted as shown in the figure indicates that no vehicle may park
130ye93.why: The yellow and black kerb means no parking, for every vehicle.

ahvk3r.q: The kerb painted as shown in the figure indicates that parking is not allowed along that stretch
ahvk3r.why: The yellow and black marks on the kerb mean no parking along that stretch.

1cide57.q: The kerb painted as shown in the figure indicates that parking is allowed only on payment
1cide57.why: The yellow and black kerb bans parking. Paid parking is marked with blue lines.

1okxpph.q: The kerb painted as shown in the figure indicates that parking is allowed for one hour only
1okxpph.why: The yellow and black kerb bans parking. Time limits are shown by signs or panels.

14an432.q: The kerb painted as shown in the figure indicates roadworks in progress
14an432.why: The yellow and black kerb means no parking, not roadworks.

1rzwhgo.q: The kerb painted as shown in the figure indicates a road with right of way
1rzwhgo.why: The yellow and black kerb means no parking. Right of way is shown by other signs.

1qmmojk.q: It is regular to find the word BUS in yellow on the road surface in areas for stopping of buses in scheduled public service
1qmmojk.why: The yellow word BUS is a regular marking in stop areas for scheduled public buses.

zl48ce.q: It is regular to find the word TAXI in yellow on the road surface to indicate zones reserved for parking of taxis in service
zl48ce.why: The yellow word TAXI marks zones reserved for taxis in service to park.

149n9cc.q: It is regular to find the word STOP on the road surface, to complement the relevant vertical sign
149n9cc.why: The word STOP on the road surface complements the vertical STOP sign.

12p09b5.q: It is regular to find the letters P L, with a St Andrew's cross, on the road surface to signal a level crossing
12p09b5.why: The letters P L with a St Andrew's cross on the road mark a level crossing (passaggio a livello).

152rg4w.q: When one meets the stripes shown in the figure painted on the road surface, one must reduce speed
152rg4w.why: Transverse stripes that get closer together are a visual speed-reduction device. They tell you to slow down.

2zg92c.q: It is regular to find the name of a place written on the road surface, to complement the directional arrow
2zg92c.why: A place name on the road surface is allowed to complement the directional arrow.

1ki9dy0.q: It is regular to find the word STOP on the road surface, to complete the vertical GIVE WAY sign
1ki9dy0.why: The word STOP complements only the STOP sign. A give-way sign uses a striped triangle on the road.

18xjo2c.q: It is regular to find the word indicating an upcoming service station on the road surface
18xjo2c.why: Only road markings written in the regulations are allowed. Announcing a service station is not one of them.

ukyylp.q: It is regular to find an advertising message on the road surface indicating a fuel station
ukyylp.why: Advertising on the road surface is not allowed. Only official traffic markings are permitted.

1my55i8.q: It is regular to find a message of encouragement for racing cyclists on the road surface
1my55i8.why: Cheering messages are not traffic markings and are not allowed on the carriageway.

ynxile.q: It is regular to find the word TAXI, in white, on the road surface in taxi parking areas
ynxile.why: The word TAXI on the road surface must be yellow, not white.

19qy955.q: It is regular to find the word GIOCHI on the road surface near public gardens
19qy955.why: The word GIOCHI (games) is not among the markings allowed on the road surface.

372wxi.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, one may overtake even by crossing the middle line
372wxi.why: The middle line is dashed, so it may be crossed. On one-way streets overtaking is allowed on either side.

kapwg4.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, one may overtake even on a bend
kapwg4.why: On a one-way street there is no oncoming traffic, so overtaking is possible even on a bend.

1yunsds.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, the carriageway is divided into two lanes
1yunsds.why: The dashed line in the middle divides the carriageway into two lanes.

1o87zpt.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, the left lane is, as a rule, reserved for overtaking
1o87zpt.why: On one-way streets too, the left lane is normally kept for overtaking.

1dl76b4.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, overtaking is allowed near or at hump-backed rises
1dl76b4.why: With no oncoming traffic, overtaking is allowed near or on a hump (dosso).

1ah072g.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, one may always travel in parallel lines
1ah072g.why: Driving in parallel lanes is allowed only when traffic density justifies it, not always.

5i2v8w.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, one may make a U-turn
5i2v8w.why: A U-turn is banned on one-way streets, because it would mean driving the wrong way.

1675ck8.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, one may drive straddling the middle line
1675ck8.why: You must stay within a lane. Driving straddling the middle line is not allowed.

1gm6od5.q: On a one-way street with the markings shown in the figure, to turn left one must stay in the right lane
1gm6od5.why: To turn left you must be in the left lane, not the right one.

8zelxc.q: The markings in the figure indicate a pedestrian crossing, both inside and outside built-up areas
8zelxc.why: Zebra stripes mark a pedestrian crossing, both inside and outside built-up areas (centri abitati).

w11ned.q: The markings in the figure indicate a pedestrian crossing that may also be found in small built-up areas
w11ned.why: A zebra crossing may also be found in small built-up areas.

1eo3svf.q: The markings in the figure indicate a pedestrian crossing
1eo3svf.why: The white parallel stripes mark a pedestrian crossing.

1in9v85.q: The markings in the figure indicate a crossing for pedestrians
1in9v85.why: The white transverse stripes mark a crossing for pedestrians.

1t5i5dz.q: The markings in the figure indicate a crossing where pedestrians have right of way
1t5i5dz.why: At a zebra crossing, pedestrians have priority over vehicles.

eo9eu5.q: The markings in the figure may be complemented by the appropriate vertical PEDESTRIAN CROSSING sign
eo9eu5.why: The zebra stripes may be complemented by the vertical pedestrian crossing sign.

1mzrgik.q: The markings in the figure oblige drivers to stop when pedestrians are crossing the carriageway
1mzrgik.why: The driver must stop when pedestrians are crossing on the stripes.

1m1wv8z.q: A pedestrian crossing may be preceded on the right by a yellow zigzag stripe, as in the following figure
1m1wv8z.why: A yellow zigzag stripe on the right may precede the crossing, as in the figure, marking a bus stop.

1ssob3g.q: The markings in the figure placed on secondary extra-urban roads must be preceded by the PEDESTRIAN CROSSING danger sign
1ssob3g.why: On secondary extra-urban roads, a pedestrian crossing must be preceded by the danger sign.

1mgmvv3.q: The markings in the figure oblige drivers to stop and give way to pedestrians who are about to cross
1mgmvv3.why: The driver must stop and give way to pedestrians crossing or about to cross.

ux3s6n.q: The markings in the figure indicate a traffic island
ux3s6n.why: These transverse stripes mark a pedestrian crossing. A traffic island (isola di traffico) has diagonal stripes.

1eib6jq.q: The markings in the figure indicate a crossing for cyclists
1eib6jq.why: A cycle crossing is marked by two dashed lines. These wide zebra stripes are for pedestrians.

139qqml.q: The markings in the figure indicate a cycle crossing
139qqml.why: A cycle crossing is marked by two dashed lines. Wide stripes like these are for pedestrians.

s074qe.q: The markings in the figure indicate a driveway entrance (passo carrabile)
s074qe.why: A driveway entrance (passo carrabile) is shown by its own no-parking sign, not by zebra stripes.

1irlnhp.q: The markings shown are a refuge island for pedestrians and cyclists.
1irlnhp.why: The parallel stripes shown are a pedestrian crossing (attraversamento pedonale), not a refuge island (isola di rifugio), which is a protected area in the middle of the road.

11nycxf.q: The markings shown do not allow vehicles to drive over them.
11nycxf.why: Vehicles may drive over a pedestrian crossing, but they must give way to pedestrians who are crossing or about to cross.

1h2aqtj.q: The markings shown indicate an area reserved only for disabled pedestrians.
1h2aqtj.why: A pedestrian crossing is for all pedestrians. Areas reserved for disabled people are marked with yellow stripes and the wheelchair symbol.

m4uh4g.q: The markings shown do not allow pedestrians to cross.
m4uh4g.why: A pedestrian crossing exists precisely so that pedestrians can cross the road, with priority over vehicles.

gwe0a5.q: The transverse white line shown can be combined with a junction regulated by a traffic light.
gwe0a5.why: The stop line marks where to stop and can go with either a traffic light or a STOP sign.

uksyxw.q: The transverse white line shown can be completed with the word STOP painted on the road surface.
uksyxw.why: The stop line can be completed by the word STOP painted on the pavement, alongside the STOP sign.

yb0thf.q: The transverse white line shown marks the point where drivers must stop when the STOP (FERMARSI E DARE PRECEDENZA) sign is present.
yb0thf.why: At a STOP sign you must halt before the stop line, which marks the exact stopping point.

8of1ke.q: The transverse white line shown marks the point where drivers must stop at a red traffic light.
8of1ke.why: At a red light the vehicle stops before the stop line, which marks where to stop.

duojia.q: The sign shown is a transverse stop line.
duojia.why: The solid transverse white line shown is the stop line (striscia di arresto).

ox9yik.q: The transverse white line shown is combined with the GIVE WAY (DARE PRECEDENZA) sign.
ox9yik.why: The stop line goes with a STOP sign or a traffic light. A give way sign uses a different marking, a dashed line (triangles).

170r3dc.q: The transverse white line shown indicates an unregulated pedestrian crossing.
170r3dc.why: A pedestrian crossing is shown by parallel stripes, not by a single solid transverse line, which is a stop line.

1vd6ndg.q: The transverse white line shown indicates a cycle crossing.
1vd6ndg.why: A cycle crossing is made of two parallel dashed lines of squares. A solid transverse line is a stop line.

ovf8a0.q: The transverse white line shown can never be crossed.
ovf8a0.why: After stopping as required, once the way is clear or the light turns green, you cross the line and continue.

fhmh8e.q: The transverse white line shown marks the start of a no-parking zone.
fhmh8e.why: The stop line only marks where to stop at a junction. A parking ban is shown by yellow lines or signs.

1e9ipce.q: On a two-way road with the markings shown, you may overtake even crossing the centre line.
1e9ipce.why: The centre line is dashed, so it may be crossed to overtake when visibility and traffic allow.

1j6ce7w.q: On a two-way road with the markings shown, you must not drive straddling the centre line.
1j6ce7w.why: Even a dashed centre line must not be driven on while straddling it. It is crossed only for manoeuvres such as overtaking.

11x7xrf.q: On a two-way road with the markings shown, to turn left you must move towards the centre of the carriageway.
11x7xrf.why: To turn left you move towards the centre of the carriageway, close to the centre line, after signalling.

1cy6tru.q: On a two-way road with the markings shown, you may overtake in any conditions of visibility and traffic.
1cy6tru.why: Overtaking is allowed only with a clear view and no danger to oncoming traffic. A dashed line does not make it always permitted.

w0gnop.q: On a two-way road with the markings shown, you may overtake even on a bend, but only in town.
w0gnop.why: On a bend visibility is limited, so overtaking is forbidden both in and outside built-up areas (centri abitati).

1ojkbv1.q: On a two-way road with the markings shown, you may make a U-turn, but without occupying the other lane.
1ojkbv1.why: A U-turn necessarily uses the opposite lane, so it cannot be done without occupying it. It is allowed only where safe and permitted.

1s6u9v2.q: On a two-way road with the markings shown, outside built-up areas the left lane is for emergency stopping.
1s6u9v2.why: The emergency lane is on the right and only on certain roads. The left lane is for driving or overtaking.

1dppym1.q: On a two-way carriageway the centre line can be solid or dashed.
1dppym1.why: The centre line can be solid or dashed, depending on whether overtaking across it is banned or allowed.

1buvvou.q: On a two-way carriageway a dashed centre line can be crossed during overtaking.
1buvvou.why: A dashed line may be crossed to overtake, if safety conditions allow.

2lkt1y.q: On a two-way carriageway the centre line may consist of two solid lines side by side, as shown.
2lkt1y.why: The centre line may be two solid lines side by side, separating the directions of travel.

1vupno0.q: On a two-way carriageway a centre line made of solid lines, as shown, allows overtaking without crossing the lines.
1vupno0.why: Solid lines may not be crossed, but overtaking is still possible if done without crossing them.

gxfo2i.q: On a two-way carriageway the centre lines shown separate the directions of travel.
gxfo2i.why: The double solid centre lines separate the two directions of travel.

j6m6ho.q: On a two-way carriageway the centre line shown can be crossed with only the left wheels.
j6m6ho.why: A solid line cannot be crossed in any way, not even with only the left wheels.

1cd9skl.q: On a two-way carriageway as shown, the centre line divides the road into two carriageways, each with two lanes.
1cd9skl.why: In the picture the centre line splits one carriageway into two lanes, one per direction, not into two carriageways.

ze4c4w.q: The solid white centre line shown divides the carriageway into two lanes.
ze4c4w.why: The solid centre line divides the carriageway into two lanes, one for each direction.

p02tva.q: The solid white centre line shown cannot be crossed.
p02tva.why: A solid line may not be crossed or driven over.

tw6pe9.q: The solid white centre line shown divides the directions of travel on two-way roads.
tw6pe9.why: The solid centre line separates the two directions of travel on two-way roads.

1lr2h29.q: The solid white centre line shown can be found on the uphill section of a crest on two-way roads.
1lr2h29.why: On the uphill part of a hump (dosso) visibility is limited, so a solid line is used to prevent overtaking.

seq60a.q: The solid white centre line shown can be found near pedestrian crossings on two-way roads.
seq60a.why: Near pedestrian crossings a solid line is used to prevent overtaking, which would be dangerous for pedestrians.

u160bw.q: The solid white centre line shown allows an overtaking manoeuvre without crossing it.
u160bw.why: Overtaking is possible if done without crossing the solid line, which may not be crossed or driven on.

fd45u8.q: The solid white centre line shown divides the road into two carriageways, each two-way.
fd45u8.why: The centre line divides one carriageway into two lanes with opposite directions, not into two two-way carriageways.

8mhowb.q: The solid white centre line shown allows driving straddling it.
8mhowb.why: A solid line may not be crossed or driven on, so you cannot drive straddling it.

95j5e1.q: The solid white centre line shown allows overtaking even by crossing it, provided only the left wheels cross.
95j5e1.why: A solid line may never be crossed, not even with only the left wheels.

1jb5037.q: The solid white centre line shown allows U-turns on two-way roads.
1jb5037.why: U-turns are forbidden over a solid line because they would require crossing it.

1jfmnqk.q: The marking shown indicates the recommended speed.
1jfmnqk.why: A number painted on the road indicates the recommended speed, here 50 km/h.

qn6q9c.q: With the marking shown, vehicles with a laden mass over 50 quintals may not pass.
qn6q9c.why: The number on the road only gives the recommended speed. It is not a mass limit.

1h7gj0v.q: The device shown is an artificial speed hump.
1h7gj0v.why: The yellow and black chevron markings show an artificial speed bump (dosso artificiale), which forces drivers to slow down.

17kfmud.q: The element shown is a speed reducer installed on the road.
17kfmud.why: The artificial bump is a speed reducer installed on the road.

5ff4px.q: The element shown represents a speed reducer.
5ff4px.why: The artificial bump shown is a speed reducer.

djc1f3.q: The element shown is placed on a stretch of road where parking is forbidden.
djc1f3.why: The artificial bump slows traffic and does not mean a parking ban.

1m32b5z.q: The element shown marks a cycle crossing.
1m32b5z.why: The bump slows vehicles. A cycle crossing is shown by two dashed lines of squares.

utmgcl.q: The element shown marks a pedestrian crossing.
utmgcl.why: The bump slows vehicles. A pedestrian crossing is made of parallel white stripes.

9p8iq1.q: The yellow boundary lines shown mark a parking area reserved for disabled people.
9p8iq1.why: The yellow lines and wheelchair symbol mark a parking space reserved for disabled people.

r7mdfc.q: The diagonal yellow stripes shown must be kept clear so disabled people can get in and out of the vehicle.
r7mdfc.why: The diagonal yellow stripes beside the bay must be left free so disabled people can get in and out of the vehicle.

10sfehv.q: The yellow stripes shown mark a parking area reserved for taxis.
10sfehv.why: Yellow stripes with the wheelchair symbol mark an area for disabled people, not for taxis.

x2g0tr.q: The yellow stripes shown mark an area reserved for loading and unloading goods.
x2g0tr.why: Here the yellow stripes with the wheelchair symbol mean an area for disabled people. Loading and unloading has its own signs.

69vsv8.q: The dashed white side line shown separates the carriageway from a lay-by.
69vsv8.why: The dashed side line separates the carriageway from a lay-by (piazzola di sosta).

1b6ajed.q: The dashed white side line shown may be crossed only in an emergency.
1b6ajed.why: Being dashed, the line can be crossed to enter and leave the lay-by. No emergency is needed.

49ha58.q: The dashed white side line shown means that parking is not possible.
49ha58.why: The lay-by is there precisely for stopping, so parking is possible.

1s2hiyg.q: The dashed white side line shown separates the carriageway from a driveway.
1s2hiyg.why: The dashed side line separates the carriageway from a driveway (passo carrabile).

1tkolnr.q: The dashed white side line shown marks the access to a cycle path.
1tkolnr.why: The dashed line separates the carriageway from a driveway, not from the access to a cycle path.

h4tk1v.q: The dashed white lines at the junction shown are guide stripes.
h4tk1v.why: The curved dashed lines in the junction are guide stripes (strisce di guida), showing the path to follow.

18eigsx.q: The white guide stripes shown do not allow turning.
18eigsx.why: Guide stripes channel and guide turns. They do not forbid them.

7eymf9.q: The dashed white side line shown separates the carriageway from an acceleration lane.
7eymf9.why: The dashed side line separates the carriageway from an acceleration lane, used for merging.

1pawrmx.q: The dashed white side line shown marks off a lay-by.
1pawrmx.why: In the picture the dashed line separates the carriageway from an acceleration lane, not a lay-by.

1xy8uiv.q: The dashed white side line shown marks the edge of the main road, separating it from the side road.
1xy8uiv.why: The dashed side line marks the edge of the main road, separating it from the side road.

17fydnk.q: The dashed white side line separates the carriageway from the emergency lane.
17fydnk.why: The emergency lane is separated from the carriageway by a solid line, not a dashed one.

1x7n3wk.q: The dashed white side line signals the start of a hard shoulder.
1x7n3wk.why: The hard shoulder (banchina) is bordered by a solid line. A dashed line separates the road from lay-bys, accesses or acceleration lanes.

dkb1ca.q: The markings shown are found near a level crossing.
dkb1ca.why: The PL sign with a St. Andrew's cross and the solid line are found near a level crossing.

gityau.q: The markings shown warn drivers that they are near a level crossing without barriers.
gityau.why: The PL markings warn of a nearby level crossing, including one without barriers.

1hfxl7z.q: The markings shown warn drivers that they are near a level crossing with barriers.
1hfxl7z.why: The PL markings warn of a nearby level crossing, including one with barriers.

q3tuji.q: With the markings shown, moving into the left part of the carriageway is not allowed.
q3tuji.why: Before a level crossing there is a solid centre line, which forbids moving to the left part of the road.

13vj8n7.q: With the markings shown, drivers must watch out for approaching trains.
13vj8n7.why: Near a level crossing drivers must watch for any approaching train.

1b1e350.q: The markings shown indicate that 150 metres ahead there is a very dangerous tram crossing.
1b1e350.why: The PL marking means a railway level crossing is near, not a tram crossing 150 metres ahead.

1x3mg9n.q: The markings shown are found only near level crossings with barriers.
1x3mg9n.why: The PL marking is found near level crossings with or without barriers.

8d8hef.q: The markings shown warn of a nearby junction controlled by local police.
8d8hef.why: The PL marking signals a level crossing, not a junction controlled by the local police.

eidbih.q: The markings shown mark off a parking area for public service buses.
eidbih.why: The PL marking does not mark a parking area. It warns of a nearby level crossing.

acvxm4.q: The emergency lane (lane A) can be used in case of vehicle breakdown, for a maximum of three hours.
acvxm4.why: In case of breakdown the emergency lane may be used, but for no more than three hours.

tl3qr3.q: The emergency lane (lane A) cannot be used for overtaking manoeuvres.
tl3qr3.why: The emergency lane may not be used for overtaking, only in a genuine need.

55nwbo.q: In the markings shown, the solid white line bordering the emergency lane (lane A) indicates a time-limited parking zone.
55nwbo.why: The solid line bordering the emergency lane does not mean a parking zone. The lane is only for stopping in case of need.

1b727vf.q: In the markings shown, the solid white line bordering the emergency lane (lane A) can always be crossed in heavy traffic.
1b727vf.why: The solid line is crossed only in a genuine emergency, not because of heavy traffic.

13qoc38.q: The emergency lane (lane A) is reserved for turning right.
13qoc38.why: The emergency lane is not for turning right. It is reserved for emergency stops.

qoe15j.q: The emergency lane (lane A) is reserved for deceleration.
qoe15j.why: The emergency lane is not for decelerating. It is reserved for stopping in case of need.

1h849hd.q: The emergency lane (lane A) is forbidden to cars but not to motorcycles.
1h849hd.why: The emergency lane is forbidden to all vehicles, motorcycles included, except in an emergency.

v5icci.q: The transverse solid line shown marks the point where you must stop at a junction regulated by a red traffic light.
v5icci.why: At a red light you stop before the solid transverse stop line.

yv1str.q: The transverse solid line shown marks the point where we must always stop at a junction if the traffic officer requires it.
yv1str.why: If a traffic officer orders a stop, you halt before the solid transverse stop line.

1e3kn2z.q: The transverse solid line shown marks the point where you must stop.
1e3kn2z.why: The solid transverse line with the word STOP marks the point where you must stop.

18hoclm.q: The transverse solid line shown marks the point where we must stop at a junction if it is unregulated.
18hoclm.why: At an unregulated junction the line does not require a stop. A stop is needed only with a STOP sign, a red light or an officer.

1pjlt52.q: The transverse solid line shown marks the point where you must always stop near a road junction.
1pjlt52.why: You do not always stop at the line. Stopping is required only with a STOP sign, a red light or an officer's order.

bimwyx.q: The transverse solid line shown means you must give way to vehicles coming from both right and left.
bimwyx.why: The solid transverse line is a stop line used with STOP or a traffic light. Giving way is shown by other signs.

stgq7y.q: The transverse solid line shown is found at the exit of a private property.
stgq7y.why: The stop line goes with junctions that have a STOP sign or traffic light, not with the exit of private property.
